blocks.text: Why Excel remains essential for compliance analysts

Compliance work is fragmented. You switch between GRC platforms, email clients, and local spreadsheets. Excel is the common language for data normalization. It allows you to merge exports from different systems to find gaps in control testing. On a Mac, you have a powerful toolset if you know how to use it correctly.
Core Excel skills for audit preparation

items: Data Validation: Use Data > Data Tools > Data Validation to restrict input. This ensures your audit logs stay clean.
Conditional Formatting: Highlight cells that violate your compliance thresholds automatically.
Pivot Tables: Use these to aggregate evidence across multiple business units.
XLOOKUP: Replace older VLOOKUP functions to match evidence files with employee lists reliably.

blocks.text: Keyboard shortcuts for faster Mac workflows

Stop using your trackpad for everything. These shortcuts keep your hands on the keyboard. Use Fn + F2 to edit a cell. Use Cmd + T to turn a range into a table instantly. Use Shift + Space to select an entire row. These small changes save minutes every single hour.

Excel supports over one million rows. However, performance drops when you hit large datasets with complex formulas. Keep your data in flat tables. Avoid using volatile functions like INDIRECT or OFFSET in large sheets. If your file slows down, save it as an .xlsb file to reduce the size.

Leaving sensitive evidence in hidden sheets that are still included in exports.
Forgetting to lock cells before sharing files with other departments.
Using inconsistent date formats that break sorting and filtering.

blocks.text: Always use the Protect Sheet feature under the Review tab. It prevents accidental changes to your formulas during the audit review process.

blocks.text: How to stay organized on macOS

Organize your folders by audit date and control ID. Use Finder tags to label files as In Progress, Ready for Review, or Final. This structure helps you find evidence quickly when an auditor asks for it. Keep your Excel files in a synced folder like iCloud or OneDrive for automatic backups.

Audit data often comes from messy exports. Use the Text to Columns feature to split names or IDs. Use the Trim function to remove extra spaces that prevent matches in your lookups. Always check for duplicates using Data > Remove Duplicates before you start your analysis.
The role of automation in compliance

While you cannot automate everything, you can reduce the manual burden. Use Power Query to connect to your data sources. This allows you to refresh your report with one click when new data arrives. It removes the need to copy and paste data manually every week.

Auditors value transparency. Add a documentation tab to your Excel files. List the source of the data, the date of the pull, and the logic behind your calculations. This reduces the number of follow-up questions you receive later. Clear notes make you look prepared and professional.

faq.question: Can I run Excel on macOS without issues?
faq.answer: Yes. Microsoft 365 for Mac is fully supported on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. Ensure you are on a supported version of macOS.

faq.question: How do I speed up slow Excel files?
faq.answer: Try removing unused formatting, deleting hidden objects, or converting your data to a binary workbook (.xlsb) format.

faq.question: Is it safe to use Lazur with confidential audit data?
faq.answer: Lazur does not store your screen content or audio. It processes your request and immediately discards the data.

faq.question: How can I compare two columns for differences?
faq.answer: You can use the IF function to compare cells or use Conditional Formatting to highlight duplicate values between columns.
